English

Generated Narrative: CodeSystem KGL2Predicates

This case-sensitive code system http://smart.who.int/base/CodeSystem/KGL2Predicates defines the following codes:

CodeDefinition
hasComponent A DAK contains one of its nine components. The qualifier carries the component name from DAK.fsh, so `dak hasComponent persona` and `dak hasComponent program-indicator` stay distinguishable when a query walks the kit.
sourcedFrom A component points at the file that defines it. TWO TARGETS ARE LICENSED, and which one an instance uses says how much is known about the file. Where a subgraph models that file type, the target is the file itself -- `business-process sourcedFrom bpmn-definitions`, licensed in l2-bpmn -- and the graph walks straight on into the file's contents. Where none does (a Gherkin feature, a FHIR canonical, or a BPMN this graph simply does not hold), the target is an l1:external-artifact carrying a URI and nothing else. Prefer the first: routing through external-artifact when the file IS modelled adds a hop through a node that, at instance level, is the same node.
realises A business process realises a user scenario. From `scenario 0..* id` on BusinessProcessWorkflow -- a bare id string, so an instance carries a resolutionStatus.
involves A user scenario involves a persona. From `personas 0..* id` on UserScenario -- again bare ids, again a resolutionStatus.
fulfilledBy A functional requirement is fulfilled by a persona. THE ONE JOIN IN THIS LAYER THAT IS NOT STRING MATCHING: the committed instances write `actor[+] = Canonical(SGAuthoring.Persona.BusinessAnalyst)`, a canonical reference that resolves without guessing. It is the counter-example that shows the other joins are a choice, not a necessity.
hasStatement A requirement carries numbered, labelled statements with a conformance verb. 170 of them exist today.
listsTask BusinessProcessWorkflow declares `task 0..*` with identifier, name and description -- the same tasks the BPMN file draws. Two representations of one list, joined by identifier, which is why dak-task exists as a node rather than a property.
references A program indicator names the health interventions that give it context. From `references 0..* id` on ProgramIndicator -- bare id strings again, so an instance carries a resolutionStatus. Distinct from derivedFrom: referencing an intervention for context is not the same claim as restating a normative indicator.
describes A DAK-level task entry describes an element of a BPMN file. Declared here and licensed in l2-bpmn, where the target class lives.
implementedBy Reused from l1, and licensed here for the L1->L2 hop that L1 could not declare itself: l1 cannot name an l2 class without a circular import, but l2 imports l1 and sees both ends. A recommendation is implemented by the DAK component that realises it. Always `inferred`, never `derived` -- deciding that a process realises a recommendation is adaptation, the judgement a DAK exists to record, and it carries a resolutionStatus like every other cross-artefact claim. Note health-intervention has NO implementedBy edge: the published SOP gives Health Interventions an L3 row of `n/a / n/a / n/a` and calls L1 recommendations inputs rather than outputs, so the trace runs through processes, decisions and indicators instead.
derivedFrom This normative content restates or operationalises that recommendation.
appearsIn A citation string appears in an L2 or L3 artefact at a stated location.
verifiedBy A requirement statement is verified by a test scenario. The statement is the granularity at which conformance is asserted, so it is also the granularity at which a test is claimed to check it. The edge records the claim that a scenario exists for the statement; whether the scenario actually exercises each success criterion is a review question, recorded per criterion by `verification` on successCriteria, not by this edge.
